summary: Re-read of the confirmed spec (Codex gpt-5.6-terra @ xhigh, read-only, task-mtx9q5l3-hubrr5) after two accepted decisions (0024, 0025) entered the product tree during planning and staled the prior requirements pass. Nine findings: seven answered by the repository and settled in the spec, two put to the human. The spec now carries a 'Settled by the requirements re-read (2026-09-11)' section recording all nine.
gaps: The settled complete-pin rule was absent from the spec: it required pinned batch ids but never one-per-loaded-month completeness, nor refusal for missing, duplicate, wrong-source or wrong-period pins, so a client could omit a month and receive an authorized but non-footing partial answer.
The pagination contract was not testable: 'server-paginated' omitted the initial page, page size and maximum, navigation metadata, invalid/out-of-range handling and the empty-result case.

The audit content had no usable record contract: AuditService.writeRequestEvent accepts a governed Selection (contract/src/measure.ts), which has no fields for a node key, resolved triples or pins, so a generic call could satisfy 'audit written' while losing the facts an investigator needs. Whether refused attempts are audited was unstated.

A vanished pinned batch had no requirement-level behaviour: replacement was covered, but a previously displayed batch that no longer exists left an implementer free to substitute the active batch and break traceability.

Exact-paise footing had no user-visible contract: the statement rounds its Actual to whole rupees, so a paise-precise footer can read up to a rupee away from the clicked cell while both are correct, and the prototype's footer claims 'Matches the Actual in the report'.
Srihari's contradictory one-level request sat as an untriggered open item with no owner, deadline or deferral entry, although it changes the core interaction.

The non-Actual rule was inconsistent: Behaviour said only Actual is interactive while the acceptance criterion and out-of-scope text named only Budget and %, omitting the Roll-over column the shipped statement actually has.
contradictions: Mapping and outline drift could break footing DESPITE a correct batch pin: the spec pins actual-batch ids but the drill re-resolves the node key to a leaf through the outline snapshot, and StatementOutlineRepository.findByBudgetPeriod filters on batch.is_active. A budget re-upload between render and click swaps the node-to-leaf mapping, so the drill reads a different row set from the correctly pinned actuals batch.

The spec's universal 'drill predicate' and audit wording permitted a server-backed aggregate drill, which accepted decision 0024 forbids: aggregates including the Grand Total are a client-only flattening of the displayed payload, and only a leaf calls the raw-transactions endpoint.
resolutions: REPO-ANSWERED — the spec now requires exactly one actuals batch per month in the clicked block's range that has one; a missing month, duplicate, wrong-source or wrong-period id is a refusal, never a partial footer. Recorded as acceptance criterion 11 in the plan.

REPO-ANSWERED — the drift contradiction is closed by pinning the BUDGET batch as well: provenance.activeBatchIds already carries source 'budget', so the drill resolves nodeKey to its leaf against the pinned outline snapshot rather than the currently-active one. The mapping master needs no pin: mis-mapping-master.ts is a compiled-in constant carrying a version (decision 0014 — no governed master in the PoC), so it cannot drift inside a running process; the audit record names its version so a deploy-time change stays traceable.

REPO-ANSWERED — the spec now states that only a leaf calls the server: every aggregate including the Grand Total is a client-side flattening that issues no request, exposes nothing new and writes no audit record, per decision 0024. An implementer must not add a server-backed aggregate drill.

REPO-ANSWERED — the pagination contract is fixed in the spec: 1-based pages, a server-fixed size of 100 that is not client-settable, total matching count plus page number and size on every response, totals over all matches, 400 for a non-integer or out-of-range page, and an empty result as a valid zero-row response with a zero footer rather than an error.

REPO-ANSWERED — the spec now defines a typed drill-audit payload (actor, node key, resolved leaf key, triples, month range, pinned actuals AND budget batch ids, mapping-master version, generated SQL, objects touched) rather than reusing the governed Selection shape.

REPO-ANSWERED — replacement and disappearance are now distinct outcomes in the spec: a batch that is no longer active but still exists is read and the replacement reported; a batch that no longer exists is refused with a distinct message. Neither falls back to the active batch.

REPO-ANSWERED — the one-level divergence is ledgered as D-0037 with a revisit trigger (demonstrated to Srihari, his async reply, or a request for a one-click group-to-transactions path), and the spec's open item now points at it.
REPO-ANSWERED — the spec now names Budget, Roll-over AND % as inert: no click handler, no focusable control, no pointer affordance.

HUMAN (kl-rahulanand) — the drill footer renders through the same rupee formatter as the statement, so 'Matches the Actual in the report' is literally true on screen, with the exact paise value on a secondary line for a user verifying to the paise. Equality is asserted in paise by the automated proof. Rejected: paise everywhere (undercuts the match claim) and rupees-only (removes the verification the feature exists for).

HUMAN (kl-rahulanand) — refused attempts are audited as well as successful reads. An authorization refusal records the actor and the predicate AS SUBMITTED under its own event type, never the resolved predicate, which would disclose what the caller could not see. Rejected: successful-only (a probe against the raw-row endpoint would leave no trace) and after-authorization-only.
open_items: Non-blocking, harness — accepting a decision during planning changes docs/decisions/, which product_tree_digest hashes, which stales the requirements grill that plan save requires. forge next step 3 instructs 'record new decisions as you go', so following the harness invalidates a gate the harness then demands. This re-read was the consequence. To be raised upstream rather than worked around.

rounds.question: The drill must foot in exact paise, but the statement cell the user clicked is rounded to whole rupees by `formatMoney` (statement-view.tsx). So the panel's footer can legitimately read ₹1 away from the number on screen while both are correct — and the prototype's footer literally says 'Matches the Actual in the report'. How should the footer display?

The audit record is written once the predicate is derived, so a drill that is refused AFTER that point (stale pin, vanished batch) is already recorded. But an attempt refused BEFORE it — no plant scope, no `report` grant, no domain — currently leaves no trace, because authorization runs first. For a surface whose whole purpose is exposing raw transaction rows, which attempts should the audit log carry?

Closing the requirements re-read. Nine findings, all settled in the spec: complete month-for-month pin; **pin the budget batch too** (a budget re-upload would otherwise swap the outline that maps node→leaf — a real footing hole neither earlier grill caught); aggregates are client-only per 0024; the pagination contract (1-based, fixed size 100, 400 on bad page, empty is valid); a typed drill-audit payload with refusals logged; vanished batch refused not substituted; footer in rupees with paise beneath; Budget/Roll-over/% all inert; and Srihari's one-level question ledgered as D-0037 with a trigger. Any remaining gap before the plan goes to the board?
options: No gaps — record and go to the board (Recommended)
The budget-batch pin needs more thought
rounds.chosen: No gaps — record and go to the board (Recommended)
